## Breaking change
This will store the value of each sensor in OpenHardwareMonitor as a float instead of a string.


## Proposed change

In some locales numbers with decimals uses "," instead of "." and this causes an issue when trying to use **InfluxDB** for example as the stored value becomes a string.
This PR fixes the issue by parsing the sensor values as a floats instead which works in all locales.

issue_context.title: Open Hardware Monitor comma should be replaced by period to be numerical value

## The problem

  The Open Hardware Monitor component pulls values in that have a comma as decimal.
  Home Assistant sees this as a non-numerical state so you can't use it for templates, graphs etc.
  A workaround for now has been to template the comma out to be a period. For example value_template: "{{ states('sensor.nuc_series_c_u_load_used_space') | replace(',','.') | float | round(0) }}".



## Environment

  
  Home Assistant 0.109.3



- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.109.3
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): None
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Home Assistant
- Integration causing this issue: Open Hardware Monitor
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/openhardwaremonitor/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```
sensor:
  - platform: openhardwaremonitor
    host: 192.168.1.99
    port: 8085
```

comments:
This seems like more of an issue with openhardware monitor. The , is used in European notations and should be covered with a configuration on that side. Unfortunately that project doesn't seem super responsive with the number of issues and pull requests.

Fixing this in HA would be a bit of a hack to fix an upstream project so unlikely to be resolved. I could be wrong and it would be fairly easy to implement a hack, but it would be just that a hack.

review_comments:
`self.value` is now a float and returned in the `state` property method.
However, states in Home Assistant are always stored as a string. Why convert it to a float first, while HA will convert it back to a string again?

Sorry, I did not know that it just converts it back to a string.

I have fixed this issue by removing the float cast and I added an extra test to show what a value can look like on a different locale.
